Why ceramic coating

Ceramic paint protection that lasts for years.

Deeper, longer-lasting gloss

A ceramic coating bonds to the clear coat and keeps paintwork looking freshly detailed for years, not the weeks a wax lasts.

Water and dirt run off

The hydrophobic surface makes rain bead and roll away, taking road dirt with it, so the car stays cleaner between washes.

Quicker, safer washing

Traffic film, bird droppings and brake dust release more easily, so washing takes less effort and less rubbing.

Protection from the elements

The coating helps shield paint from UV, road salt and contamination that dull the finish over time.

A ceramic coating isn't scratch-proof and doesn't replace careful washing. Our ceramic coating aftercare guide explains how to keep it performing.

Our process

How we apply your ceramic coating.

Everything happens inside our climate-controlled detailing studio at Consensus House, Norwich, so the coating goes onto clean, dry, dust-free paint.

  1. 1

    Decontamination wash

    A safe pre-wash and contact wash with our Kranzle K7, then iron fallout and tar removal and a clay bar treatment to take off bonded contamination.

  2. 2

    Spotless-water rinse

    Rinsing with our inline spotless-water system reduces the minerals that leave water marks, so the paint is genuinely clean before it is inspected.

  3. 3

    Inspection and panel preparation

    The paint is checked under our studio lighting, then every panel is prepared so the coating bonds properly. Paint correction is carried out first where it's booked.

  4. 4

    Gyeon ceramic coating

    The coating is applied panel by panel indoors, out of the wind, rain and dust, and levelled for an even, glossy finish.

  5. 5

    Curing and final check

    The coating is left to cure in the studio, then we carry out a final inspection and talk you through aftercare at handover.

Ceramic coating FAQs

Your questions answered.

How much does ceramic coating cost in Norwich?

Our ceramic coating packages start from £445 for the 3 + 1 Year Ceramic Coating (4 years of protection) and £495 for the 7-Year Ceramic Coating with a Clay Bar Decontamination Wash. Prices depend on vehicle size, from small city cars to large SUVs, 4x4s and vans, up to £895 for paint correction plus a 7-year coating on an extra-large vehicle. Every package price includes the preparation the coating needs.

How long does ceramic coating last?

Choose 4 years (the 3 + 1 Year package: a 3-year coating plus a second coat the next day for an extra year) or 7 years (our 7-year packages). How long it lasts in practice depends on safe washing and aftercare; we give you aftercare advice at handover.

How long will you need my car?

The 7-Year Ceramic Coating with Clay Bar Decontamination Wash is about 10 working hours, so we keep the vehicle until the next working day. The 3 + 1 Year package needs a full working day plus about 2 hours the following day for the second coat. A loan car or van can be requested when you book.

Does my car need paint correction before a ceramic coating?

Not always. New cars and well-kept paint only need our full decontamination and preparation, which every package includes. If the paint has swirls, haze or light scratches, choose Paint Correction + 7-Year Ceramic so the finish is corrected before it is protected. We inspect the paint before starting and talk you through it.

Can you ceramic coat alloy wheels and convertible roofs?

Yes. Wheel faces can be coated on the car (from £195) or with the wheels off so the barrels are protected too (from £280). Fabric soft tops can be deep cleaned and coated (from £95). These are added to a suitable main service.

Is ceramic coating better than wax?

A ceramic coating bonds to the paint and lasts years, where wax lasts weeks to months. It keeps paint glossier, makes it repel water and dirt, and makes washing quicker. It isn't scratch-proof, and it still needs safe washing. Our ceramic coating vs car wax guide compares the two in detail. Read the guide.

Which ceramic coating do you use?

We use Gyeon ceramic coatings, applied by hand in our indoor, climate-controlled Norwich studio after a full decontamination wash and panel preparation.
